title: Nivat's conjecture
abstract: Formalizes the proof of Nivat's conjecture found by GPT-6 Pro. A configuration on the integer lattice over a finite alphabet whose number of distinct patterns on some m-by-n rectangle is at most m times n has a nonzero period. Develops rational alphabet labelings, the Laurent-polynomial shift action and its annihilator ideals, the exact line ideal of a half-plane-supported difference of orbit-closure points, complexity descent to a smaller rectangle, and Szabados's two-factor theorem for finite-range configurations.

informal.Nivat.nivat: For every finite alphabet A and configuration c from the integer lattice to A, if for some positive m and n the number of distinct patterns of c on the m-by-n rectangle, counted over all integer translations, is at most m times n, then there is a nonzero lattice vector h with c(z + h) = c(z) for every z.
informal.NivatSubmission.nivat: The same statement written with Mathlib vocabulary only, as registered with Palomar. The pattern set is the range of the restriction of translates of c to the product of the integer intervals [0, m) and [0, n), its natural cardinality is at most m times n, and the conclusion is a lattice vector h different from (0, 0) with c(z + h) = c(z) for all z.
informal.Nivat.nivat_rational: A finite-range rational-valued configuration whose pattern count on some m-by-n rectangle with m, n positive is at most m times n is periodic. This is proved by strong induction on the area of the rectangle.
informal.Nivat.two_factors: If a finite-range rational configuration has pattern count at most m times n on an m-by-n rectangle with m, n positive and is annihilated by the product of two difference operators in nonzero directions h and t, then it is periodic.
informal.Nivat.Descent.exists_smaller_low_complex: If two pointwise limits x and y of translates of a finite-range rational configuration c have nonzero difference whose Laurent annihilator ideal is generated by a nonzero polynomial, and c has pattern count at most m times n on an m-by-n rectangle, then applying that polynomial to c yields a configuration with pattern count at most its area on some rectangle of strictly smaller positive area.
informal.Nivat.Algebra.exact_line_in_basis: A nonzero rational configuration that vanishes on the open lower half-plane of a lattice basis and is periodic with positive period q along the first basis direction has Laurent annihilator ideal generated by a single line-supported polynomial, obtained from a monic divisor of X^q - 1 of positive degree.
